reasoning:
The claim that mRNA COVID-19 vaccines can alter or permanently change human DNA is scientifically false and has been thoroughly debunked by medical and scientific authorities, including the Mayo Clinic, the CDC, and the World Health Organization. 

Under basic biological principles, mRNA (messenger RNA) from the vaccines does not enter the nucleus of the cell, which is where human DNA is housed. Furthermore, human cells do not possess the necessary enzymes, such as reverse transcriptase, to convert the vaccine's mRNA back into DNA. The mRNA delivered by the vaccine acts as a temporary set of instructions for the cell's cytoplasm to produce the spike protein, after which the cell naturally and quickly breaks down and disposes of the mRNA.
title: mRNA vaccines alter human DNA
